title: Redline escalation handoff — March 9 2027 (dawn shift)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the active Redline escalation that started in the early hours of 2027-03-09 (UTC), the actions taken so far, current system state, and recommended next steps for the incoming on-call. Use this during the bridge transfer and add notes inline.

Executive summary:
- Severity: Redline (P1) — production traffic impacted; multiple customers reporting 5xx and high tail latency for text-generation endpoints in eu-west-1 and us-east-1.
- Primary symptom: sudden increase in 5xx errors from request-router -> serving-runtime with correlated spike in request tail latency.
- Impact: ~12% of live requests failed with HTTP 502/504 between 02:03–02:28 UTC; elevated latency persisted for another hour for smaller fraction.
- Current status: mitigations applied (partial fallback routing, temporary capacity scale-up); active mitigations holding but root cause not confirmed. Monitoring watch remains.

Key contacts (pager escalation):
- Primary SRE: Maya Chen (pager)
- Secondary SRE: Jonah Martinez (pager)
- Infra lead: Priya Singh (slack/pager)
- Serving Runtime owner: Luca Romano (slack)
- Product EM for Hosted API: Allison Park (slack)

Immediate actions performed (chronological):
1) 02:01 UTC — Alerts fired: surge in 5xx rate for /v1/generate (eu-west-1). Pager jumped to SRE.
2) 02:05 UTC — On-call executed quick health checks: router pods healthy, nginx error logs showed upstream timeouts to serving-runtime.
3) 02:07 UTC — Scaled serving-runtime deployment in eu-west-1 by +30% (manual override) to bring up additional workers.
4) 02:12 UTC — Noted increased Redis cache miss rate and eviction spikes on cache-proxy-eu-1.
5) 02:15 UTC — Enabled routing fallback: route 10% of traffic to dedicated-capacity-pool fallback and 15% to model-variant-v0.9 (more conservative memory footprint).
6) 02:22 UTC — Error rate dipped but tail latency still high for sequences >1024 tokens.
7) 02:35 UTC — Observed a gradual removal of a small set of unhealthy GPU nodes in gpu-pool-2 (OOM / driver-reset events). Restarted nodes and cordoned one for investigation.
8) 03:05 UTC — Opened INC-2027-58 (Jira) and started a Redline bridge.

What we believe happened (hypothesis):
- The most likely chain: a sudden workload shift (large-batch long-context requests) caused memory pressure on a subset of GPU nodes. This triggered OOM/driver resets that led to upstream timeouts from serving-runtime. Simultaneously, the KV prefix cache saw a spike in evictions which increased cold-start costs and forced additional CPU work in model preparation paths.
- Contributing factor: an aggressive cache TTL/eviction policy combined with a recent optimization (PR #842) that changed kernel selection heuristics for sequences >1024. That optimization may increase transient memory pressure for certain model variants.

Current system state (as of 04:45 UTC):
- Alerts: degraded but firing at reduced rates; 5xx rate back down to ~1.7% (baseline ~0.2%).
- Routing: fallback policy still active (20% traffic to dedicated pool + variant fallback).
- GPU pool: 2 nodes cordoned in gpu-pool-2; 4 nodes restarted and healthy.
- Cache: cache-proxy-eu-1 eviction rate stable but elevated (~3x baseline).
- Customer-facing UX: UX errors reduced after fallback; support notified via CS.

Evidence collected / logs to review: (quick pointers)
- Request traces: trace IDs sampled around 02:00–02:30 show latency stacking at model-init step (trace examples: trace-7e3a, trace-9b2c).
- Serving-runtime logs (eu-west-1, pod sr-worker-5): repeated kernel allocation failures and driver reset entries at 02:18–02:24.
- GPU metrics: per-GPU memory usage hit 98% for small subset; swap-to-disk events logged.
- Redis metrics: cache-proxy evictions spiked; redis INFO shows 'evicted_keys' jump.
- PR to review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842 (kernel selection change).

Temporary mitigations applied (still in place):
- Traffic fallback: 20% to dedicated-capacity (manual routing config).
- Model variant fallback: traffic split to model-variant-v0.9 for long context requests.
- Scale up: manual +30% serving-runtime replica increase in impacted region.
- Node management: cordoned problematic GPU nodes; lifecycle team investigating driver logs.

Runbook edits recommended (urgent):
- Update the "GPU OOM and driver-reset" runbook section to include: check kernel-selection PRs made in last 48 hours and a checklist to quickly revert that config.
- Add quick check in the "cache-proxy" runbook: a command to dump top keys by size and current eviction rate (sample command included below).
- Add a routing rollback snippet for the Canary fallback (how to revert traffic split safely).

Commands / snippets used during this incident (paste to use):
- kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=sr-worker -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running
- kubectl -n serving logs sr-worker-5 -c runtime | sed -n '1,200p'
- redis-cli -h cache-proxy-eu-1 INFO | egrep "evicted_keys|used_memory_human|maxmemory"
- curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <o>' https://router.eu-west-1.redwood/v1/health -sS -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code} TIME:%{time_total}\n"

Open action items (who / what / status):
- [Maya] Continue bridge until metrics stable for 60m (in progress).
- [Jonah] Deep-dive into kernel-selection changes in PR #842, reproduce memory footprint locally (in progress).
- [Priya] Validate GPU driver logs with infra team and open infra-level RCA if driver fault confirmed (assigned).
- [Luca] Prepare rollback plan for model-variant routing and a staged rollback script (in progress).
- [Customer Success] Communicate interim status to top 10 customers that reported issues (requested).

Notes for incoming on-call:
1) Bridge invite is active (see linked_confluence above). Join the short sync every 15 minutes until the metric thresholds are stable.
2) If 5xx rate rises above 5% again, flip fallback to 50% and escalate to infra lead immediately.
3) If another GPU node OOMs, cordon the node and increase fallback to 75% (this is to avoid cascading driver resets).
4) Keep an eye on cache-proxy evictions; if eviction rate >10x baseline, revert PR #842 in the canary lane.

Suggested post-incident work (postmortem/backlog):
- Full RCA to determine whether kernel-selection change increased transient memory peaks. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Add canary load tests for long-context workloads to catch memory-pressure regressions. Owner: perf-team.
- Tune cache-proxy eviction policy and add alerting for eviction rate >5x baseline. Owner: infra/cache team.
- Improve automatic fallbacks: automate detection of GPU-driver-reset patterns and auto-divert traffic. Owner: platform-engineering.

Appendix — quick diagnostics output (captured snippets):
- redis INFO excerpt: "used_memory_human:1257.81M\nmaxmemory:1342177280\nevicted_keys:1423"
- recent kernel allocation error (serving-runtime): "Allocation failed: requested 104857600 bytes, available 82354304"
- sample trace timeline: 02:14:02 request received -> 02:14:22 model-init start -> 02:15:01 kernel alloc fail -> 02:15:06 upstream timeout returned to client

Last note: this escalation stabilized after routing fallbacks and node restarts, but the underlying memory-pressure hypothesis needs confirmation before we close the Redline. If you make changes, annotate this doc with timestamped notes and update INC-2027-58.

-- Maya (on-call)
